action_items: (No blockers) — the PDF viewer works end-to-end on web preview. Consider adding a native-only manual verification once you produce an EAS build: on Android the WebView wraps the PDF with Google Docs Viewer (docs.google.com/gview?embedded=true&url=…), which requires the file to be publicly reachable; since /file requires a JWT query param the URL IS reachable but the token leaks into Google's referer chain. Long-term: sign a short-lived download URL (e.g. 60s) and pass THAT to Google's viewer, so the master JWT never touches a third-party host.
(Carry-over from iter_3) server.py grew to 1439 lines — split into routers (auth/library/ai/…) and migrate deprecated on_event('shutdown') to FastAPI lifespan events.
critical_code_review_comments: app/library/pdf/[bookId].tsx passes the raw JWT as a query param to Google Docs Viewer on Android — Google will retain that URL in its access logs. Consider a signed short-TTL download token instead of the primary JWT.

The /library/books/{book_id}/file endpoint returns the entire ~55MB body via Response(content=...) which loads it fully into RAM per request. For hot books this is fine but not scalable — switch to StreamingResponse (or FileResponse if you can persist to disk) and honor Range requests so browser/WebView PDF viewers can seek without downloading the whole file.

get_object(b['storage_path']) is called via run_in_threadpool but there's no ETag / Cache-Control / Content-Length header set — every reader reload re-transfers 55MB. Add ETag = sha256(storage_path+updated_at) and Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.

PdfViewer uses `useEffect(() => { getToken(); })` and passes the token in URL. If the token expires while the user is reading, the iframe silently 401s. Consider surfacing a friendly 'session expired, please tap Read Original PDF again' state on iframe error.
